source_comparison: ASP implementation, the three benchmark names, domain independence and the safety-critical driving example are preserved. The source keyword list is omitted.
Both kernels, their distinct roles, SCK(+), evaluation settings and the EPN subspace-detection result are retained.
Both attention networks, their combination, and all three application tasks remain explicit.
The framework, corpus construction, benchmark and automated system remain distinct. The two priority claims are attributed to the authors.
The adversarial training mechanism, two fairness measures and qualified performance trade-off are retained.
Bilingual and multilingual support, corpus-based model building, inference and JIT export are present. The unusual word “vaulted” also occurs in the source.
Graph composition, the MLJ syntax, and out-of-sample base predictions in stacking are preserved.
The three solver interfaces are named, and repeated validation is tied to editing.
Preserves concentration of alignment probability, simpler decoding, retained word error rate and improved alignment.
Preserves dynamic modality weighting and the pseudo-label prior. The superiority claim stays limited to LLP.
Multi-particle walks, learned dynamics operators, and classification and regression evaluations are present.

The abstract preserves the ensemble, ADAM ranking and public release. The source title explicitly identifies extreme class imbalance, which disappears from the candidate title and abstract. Suggested title: Loss Ensembles for Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation Under Extreme Class Imbalance.
The abstract retains practical adoption, the three review topics, tools and future directions.
All six named languages and both multilingual and cross-lingual settings are preserved.
All four generalization axes and the nine-task benchmark remain explicit. The draft attributes leading results to structural prompting generally.
Preserves the derivation, both gradient approaches and the unresolved efficiency question.
Keeps the three objectives and limits the reported trade-off to some benchmarks.
